summary: Oman lets GCC nationals enter freely and waives visas for short visits by around 80 nationalities — including the EU, US, UK and Canada, for stays of up to 14 days — while the Royal Oman Police eVisa covers longer tourist stays; other nationalities need a sponsored or embassy visa.

AF.notes: Not eligible for unsponsored entry. A visit visa must be arranged through a sponsor in Oman (hotel, employer or relative) or an Omani embassy before travel.

AL.notes: Visa-free entry for stays of up to 14 days. A return ticket, accommodation and health insurance are formally required; for longer visits apply for the Royal Oman Police eVisa and confirm current eligibility on evisa.rop.gov.om before travel.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Oman — Entry visas (14-day visa exemption, first and second groups)

DZ.notes: Visa needed unless you qualify for the 14-day exemption: citizens of this country who live in, or hold a valid visa for, the US, Canada, Australia, the UK, a Schengen country or Japan, or who live in a GCC country in an eligible profession, can enter visa-free for up to 14 days (not extendable) with a return ticket, hotel booking, health insurance and enough funds. Otherwise arrange a visa through a sponsor or check options on evisa.rop.gov.om.

conditionalWaivers.text: Residents of another GCC state can apply for Oman's GCC-resident eVisa (four weeks, extendable by one week) instead of a sponsored visa, provided the residence permit is valid for at least six more months. Oman restricts this route to residents in listed professional categories. Check your profession on the Royal Oman Police eVisa portal first.

source.name: Royal Oman Police eVisa — visa types (Visit Unsponsored visas: GCC Resident Visa, type 29)

conditionalWaivers.text: Citizens of the Foreign Ministry's second group of countries (among them India, Egypt, Morocco, Mexico and Vietnam) can enter Oman visa-free for up to 14 days if they live in, or hold a valid visa for, the United States, Canada, Australia, the United Kingdom, a Schengen country or Japan, or live in a GCC country in a profession eligible for the resident visa. The stay cannot be extended, and a return ticket, hotel booking, health insurance and enough funds are required.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Oman — Entry visas (14-day visa exemption, first and second groups)

source.name: Frequently Asked Questions - Evisa

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from travelers aged nine months and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, and a transit of more than 12 hours through such a country's airport counts. Oman applies its own list of origin countries rather than WHO's risk list.

source.name: WHO, International Travel and Health, Annex 1 — countries requiring proof of vaccination against yellow fever
source.instrument: International Health Regulations (2005), Article 36 and Annex 7; WHO International Travel and Health, Annex 1, 18 November 2022 (revised 3 January 2023)

travelInsurance.text: Visa-free entry formally requires health insurance covering the stay, alongside a return ticket and accommodation booking — checks are inconsistent, but carry proof.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Oman travel advice: entry requirements

onwardTicket.text: Visa-free visitors must hold a confirmed return or onward ticket and may be asked for proof of accommodation.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Oman travel advice: entry requirements

proofOfFunds.text: Visa-free visitors must carry enough money to cover their living costs during the stay. Oman publishes no fixed amount.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Oman — Entry visas

currencyLimits.text: Cash, bearer securities, precious metals or gemstones worth OMR 6,000 or more (or the foreign-currency equivalent) must be declared to customs on arrival and on departure, on the money-laundering declaration form.

source.name: Oman Customs (Royal Oman Police) — traveller services
source.instrument: Law on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing, Article 53

notes: Non-Muslim adult travelers arriving by air may import a small amount of alcohol for personal use — drinking in public is illegal.
Drones require prior authorization from the Civil Aviation Authority and are otherwise held at the airport until departure.

payments.text: Cards are accepted in hotels, malls and most restaurants in Muscat and Salalah; carry some rial cash for souqs, taxis, fuel stations and rural areas.

safety.text: Crime in Oman is very low, but the FCDO reports strikes and retaliatory attacks by Iran in Oman, among other places in the region, since 8 July 2026, and warns of flight cancellations and short-notice airspace closures. Stay away from military and security sites, respect local laws and customs, and take care in wadis, which flood after heavy rain from October to March.

source.name: UK FCDO — Oman travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: October to April is warm and pleasant for Muscat, the mountains and the desert; June to September brings extreme heat except in Salalah, where the khareef monsoon turns Dhofar green.

idp.text: Oman is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: Oman is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Oman yet.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

tips.text: The 14-day visa-free entry is for genuine short visits and formally requires a return ticket, accommodation and health insurance — for longer trips apply for the 30-day eVisa on the Royal Oman Police portal before travel.
Flash floods in wadis are Oman's biggest hazard for visitors — never enter, camp in or drive through a wadi when rain is forecast anywhere upstream, even under blue sky where you stand.
A 4x4 is legally required for some mountain roads, including the ascent to Jebel Shams and Jebel Akhdar, where police checkpoints turn back two-wheel-drive cars.
Dress modestly in public — shoulders and knees covered is the safe rule in towns, souqs and mosques; swimwear belongs only at hotel pools and beaches.
Alcohol is served only in licensed hotels and restaurants — drinking in public and drink-driving are criminal offenses with zero tolerance.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Oman?
faq.answer: GCC nationals enter freely. Around 80 nationalities — including the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, Japan and China — can enter visa-free for up to 14 days, provided they hold a return ticket, accommodation and health insurance. For longer tourist stays the Royal Oman Police issues an unsponsored 30-day eVisa. Other nationalities need a sponsored or embassy visa.

faq.question: How does Oman's 14-day visa-free entry work?
faq.answer: Eligible nationalities are admitted without a visa for stays of up to 14 days at all entry points. The waiver formally requires a confirmed return ticket, an accommodation booking and health insurance, though checks vary. It is intended for single short visits — for anything longer, apply for the eVisa before travel and confirm current eligibility on evisa.rop.gov.om.

faq.question: How much does the Oman eVisa cost?
faq.answer: The unsponsored tourist eVisa costs OMR 5 for a 10-day visit or OMR 20 for 30 days (extendable once). Apply only through the Royal Oman Police portal at evisa.rop.gov.om and confirm the exact fee during the application.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Oman?
faq.answer: Oman has no diplomatic relations with Israel and does not currently admit travelers on Israeli passports. Confirm with an Omani embassy before making any plans, as policy can change. Israeli stamps in other passports are not generally an obstacle to entering Oman.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Oman?
faq.answer: October to April, when coastal and desert temperatures are pleasant. The exception is the Dhofar region around Salalah, which is at its most spectacular during the khareef monsoon from roughly June to September, when the hills turn green while the rest of Arabia bakes.
